plugins.name: parallelguard
plugins.description: Per-session concurrency cap for Claude Code. A PreToolUse hook counts the Bash calls and subagents actually in flight for this session and denies the call that would exceed the cap (3 concurrent shells and 3 concurrent subagents by default; HARNESS_MAX_PARALLEL may lower it, never raise it); PostToolUse returns the slot and the ledger is cleared at every turn boundary. Two pools rather than one, because a single shared pool deadlocks: a subagent holds its slot for its whole lifetime, so with the cap's worth of subagents live, every Bash call those same subagents make would be denied. Cannot-determine denies (unparseable payload, unreadable ledger, unavailable lock, failed write, panic, missing platform binary) because a PreToolUse hook that exits 0 with no output IS an allow — and every deny is recoverable without a human (turn-boundary reset, 30s stale-lock steal). Enforcement lives in a bundled binary, not in prose a model may ignore. Subscription-native (no API key).

plugins.name: blastguard
plugins.description: v0.2.61 corrects a docstring in the axis v0.2.60 added, which claimed the relative-path case was handled when it is not: cd /etc && echo x > paths.d/evil is ALLOW, was ALLOW on the preceding commit too, and is tracked in backlog f1c170ab. v0.2.60 filled in the second axis that v0.2.59's recoverability rewrite left open. Recoverability answers "are these bytes recoverable after they are gone?", which is the right question for a file whose CONTENT is at risk and the wrong one for a file whose EXISTENCE is the payload: /etc/sudoers.d/evil, /etc/paths.d/evil and /Library/LaunchDaemons/evil.plist do not exist, so the probe answered NothingToDestroy - truthfully - and the truncating-redirect rule continued past them into Allow. Measured on the deployed 0.2.59 binary all three were allowed; all three were denied by 0.2.58. scope::is_inside_system_dir is that reserved second axis, which reversible.rs's own module doc already named ("Recoverability is not the only reason to surface a command ... callers must consult it FIRST"). It denies rather than asks, because the ambiguity that makes Ask honest for a gate-config path - only the human knows whether an edit strengthens or disarms it - has no counterpart when an agent installs into /etc. Both the truncating and the APPEND redirect loops consult it, since one appended line is a whole paths.d entry. The system list is deliberately narrower than scope::NEVER_A_ROOT: /home, /Users, /Volumes and /mnt are excluded because denying every absolute write under them would re-create the friction 0.2.59 measured and retired, and /var is excluded because the macOS per-user $TMPDIR lives there. A target confined to a safe root still escapes, so a project checked out at /opt/myproj is unaffected.

plugins.name: backlog
plugins.description: v0.3.3 corrects a factual claim inside v0.3.2's note, in place: the orphaned settings.json entry was described as hand-edited, but it is `backlog install`'s own output (src/install.rs binary_path() -> std::env::current_exe(), command_group(..., 5) -> the timeout 5 the live entry carries). The provenance matters because it names the mechanism: a plugin subcommand that writes an absolute binary path into user settings will rot every time that binary moves, and it is not fixed by anyone being more careful. Prose only. v0.3.2 moves the SessionStart hook DECLARATION into the plugin (hooks/hooks.json -> ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/backlog session-start). src/hooks/session_start.rs has existed since the crate did, and this description already claimed "a SessionStart hook that surfaces pending work at session open", but hooks/hooks.json never existed (`git log -- crates/backlog/hooks` is empty): the only wiring was an absolute path in the operator's ~/.claude/settings.json pointing at ~/.cargo/bin/backlog session-start. That path was not hand-written: it is `backlog install`'s own output -- src/install.rs's binary_path() bakes std::env::current_exe() into settings.json and command_group(..., 5) writes the timeout 5 that the live entry carries verbatim. The plugin was writing its own guaranteed-to-rot wiring. That binary was renamed to backlog.bak-stale-20260820 on 2026-08-20, so the hook has exited 127 (No such file or directory) on every session since. A SessionStart hook has no exit code and no stderr the agent ever sees, so it did not go red, it went DARK: "the queue is empty" and "the hook never ran" became indistinguishable downstream, which is the same false-empty CLAUDE.md sections 1 and 3 name and that v0.2.20's divergence module exists to prevent one level down. Measured 2026-08-26 at 58c779af: the first restored run requeued 24 expired deferred tasks in one go -- requeue_expired had been stopped for the same period. The timeout is 10s rather than the old settings.json 5s, because the tasks-file lock's blocking-acquire budget is a measured 8s (see v0.2.27) and 5s could kill a legitimate lock wait midway. A new test (tests/session_start_hook_wired.rs, RED observed before the fix) pins both that the declaration exists and that it resolves through ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} rather than .cargo/bin, so the wiring travels with the rollout and cannot be orphaned by a renamed, bumped, or absent binary. The same commit also fixes a terminal-status bug in store::requeue_expired that the restored hook immediately exposed: of the 24 tasks its first run moved, 8 were `done` and 6 were `cancelled` (including 100af807, which CLAUDE.md cites as landed in d30d9b00). defer_until is only ever cleared inside requeue_expired and never on a terminal transition, so a task deferred once and later finished keeps a past defer_until forever, and the requeue branch forced status = pending without consulting status at all (store::requeue_expired; the guard now sits at crates/backlog/src/store.rs:1151). done and cancelled tasks are now left ENTIRELY untouched -- the stale field is inert because next and is_pending already exclude those statuses, and not normalising it means a completion timestamp is never re-stamped and the count the hook reports never covers work it did not move. failed is deliberately NOT terminal: `fail --defer` is the retry-later path and its expiry returning to pending is the point (requeue_expired_restores_pending). Re-measured against the same store, the run moves 24 -> 10 tasks (8 failed deferrals plus the 2 stale claims CA-backlog-005 rescues). A new unit test (requeue_expired_leaves_done_and_cancelled_terminal, RED observed before the fix) pins it, keeping failed and pending as anti-vacuity controls so an implementation that requeues NOTHING cannot pass. v0.3.1 anchors v0.3.0's cited counts to their measurement points and ships the re-measurement command, after re-running it showed the store had already moved (258/66/5 pending-or-failed rows by label at bb046648, 265/70/5 at 89feaddb, both 2026-08-20) -- exactly the drift CLAUDE.md's measurement rule exists to catch. Both readings are stated with their own rev instead of one silently overwriting the other. Docs and comments only; no behaviour change. v0.3.0 scopes the queue to the project you are standing in, in both directions (backlog 81dfaae4 / 7d8ab7fe). A repo store (<repo root>/.backlog/tasks.toml) is a tracked file that by construction holds that repo's tasks, but reads ALSO filtered rows by the writing checkout's absolute path, so one repo's queue split into one queue per machine: pending-or-failed rows by label were 258 under the macOS checkout path and 66 under the WSL one at measurement point bb046648 (2026-08-20), each invisible from the other; re-measured at 89feaddb the same day they were 265 and 70 (see crates/backlog/README.md for the command). The row filter is gone for a repo store -- the file IS the scope -- and --project becomes an ASSERTION about which store the caller meant: naming this repo changes nothing, naming a different one is a non-zero exit with the reason, never a filtered listing ("this store is a different project" and "this project has nothing queued" must not render the same, CLAUDE.md section 3). The write side asserts the same thing, since a row written here under another repo's label would now be listed as this repo's work; a PROVEN mismatch is refused, while an identity that could not be checked still files the task and carries the uncertainty as data (project_unresolved = true, rendered as [project unresolved: ...]) because a blocked add loses the finding being filed. Second half: a cwd with no repo root above it no longer falls back to the cross-project ~/.backlog. That fallback is how a process running in a tempdir wrote its fixtures into the operator's real queue (specforge spec-ratify tasks found under project="/tmp/.tmpsYSvwG") and how a read from such a cwd was answered with another project's work; config::StoreLocation makes "there is no project store here" expressible, and add/list/next refuse with the reason plus the store_dir escape hatch. divergence::check now takes the two stores' scopes separately: counting the resolved store under a filter its reader no longer applies would let Undetermined (non-zero exit, empty stdout) fire on a listing that held real work, which is the false-empty that module exists to prevent. Six new contract tests plus two controls in tests/project_scope.rs; the eleven existing tests that pinned the old filter or the old fallback are re-pinned in place, each stating which way it went and why. Cross-project task queue with cycle-type tags for Claude Code: a /backlog skill that loops through open items (lock → pick → /condukt → done), a SessionStart hook that surfaces pending work at session open, and a backlog binary with list/next/done/fail/lock subcommands. v0.2.27 stops the tasks-file lock from reaping a LIVE holder (backlog d7e1ac30). Reaping was keyed on lockfile mtime age alone, but nothing refreshes that mtime after create_new sets it, so "old" measured how long the CURRENT holder had held the lock, not whether it had died: any waiter arriving after a live holder passed the 10s window removed that holder's lockfile and took the lock, and both parties then ran read-modify-write on tasks.toml believing they held it exclusively (the bd6d81df lost update). The acquire path now records the holder's pid and reaping requires BOTH an old lockfile AND a holder confirmed gone; an unreadable/unparseable holder is Unknown and is never reaped, since "I could not tell whether the holder is alive" must not be spent as permission to steal mutual exclusion (CLAUDE.md section 3). A crashed holder is still recovered, proven by an anti-vacuity control that reaps a lockfile whose process really exited. The blocking-acquire budget is also now MEASURED ELAPSED WALL-CLOCK TIME (8s) instead of an attempt count times a sleep: the old arithmetic counted only the sleep and ignored the per-attempt syscall and stat, so the documented "about 8s" budget really ran 9.967965208s against a 10s stale window -- a 0.03s margin, not the comfortable margin the prose claimed. v0.2.22 makes `next --claim` mutually exclusive across CHECKOUTS, not just across processes sharing one store file (backlog 709ff549): the store follows the checkout by design (<repo root>/.backlog/tasks.toml, a linked worktree counting as its own root per CLAUDE.md section 8), but the claim's exclusion was keyed on that resolved STORE PATH, so two checkouts of one project took two disjoint locks over two diverged files and both were handed the SAME task id (measured: 17 checkouts, 10 distinct store sizes). A machine-global claim ledger at ~/.backlog/claims/<project-slug>.json - keyed by the same project IDENTITY hash `backlog lock` already uses, which normalizes a linked worktree to its main working tree - is now read and written inside a project-scoped critical section taken BEFORE the per-store tasks-file lock. Every undetermined condition on the claim path REFUSES the claim and exits non-zero with the reason on stderr (ledger dir not creatable, ledger lock not acquired, ledger unreadable/unparseable/unwritable, tasks-file lock not held, project identity unresolvable); the claim now returns Determination<Option<Task>> so a refusal is no longer spelled Ok(None), which main.rs used to render as `no pending tasks` on exit 0 - a driver reads that as "there is no work". v0.2.20 makes "the queue is empty" distinguishable from "you are reading a different store" (backlog 5ba13c3e criterion 2): the per-repo store migration left the legacy ~/.backlog/tasks.toml behind, so a pre-migration checkout got an ordinary `no tasks` / `[]` while 490 items (three p0s) sat in the old file — "could not observe your queue" rendered as "there is nothing to do" (CLAUDE.md §3). A new divergence module answers with three values: an ABSENT legacy store (fresh clone) stays completely silent, an UNREADABLE one is never concluded to be empty, and a resolved store holding no queued work for this project while the legacy store holds some makes `list`/`next` exit non-zero with the reason on stderr instead of printing an empty result (autoflow::backlog::find_open reads that as Determination::Undetermined and blocks the Stop visibly). When the resolved store DOES hold work the listing still exits 0 and only warns that it is incomplete — escalating there would erase real items from consumers that map a non-zero exit to "none" (overwatch's shell_soft -> `(none)`, condukt's `2>/dev/null || true`), manufacturing the very false-empty being fixed. The SessionStart hook injects the notice into additionalContext, its only channel to the agent. v0.2.10: adds probe_path_env_lock_actually_serializes_concurrent_holders, a deterministic proof that PROBE_PATH_ENV_LOCK actually serializes holders (F->P oracle for the v0.2.9 fix). v0.2.9: store.rs のテストに PROBE_PATH_ENV_LOCK を追加し、real-git-init テストと PATH-hijack テストの並列実行レースを解消。 v0.2.8 bounds `git_remote_origin_url`'s `git config --get remote.origin.url` invocation with a 5s timeout (harness_core::boundary::run_with_timeout) instead of spawning it unbounded via a raw `Command::output()`, since a hung `git` (corrupt/locked index, wedged credential helper, stuck fsmonitor/hook subprocess) could otherwise block the `Add` command's caller indefinitely; a timeout (like any other git failure) now fails soft to an empty remote URL, same as today. v0.2.7 bounds `gh_probe`'s `gh` invocation with a 20s timeout (harness_core::boundary::run_with_timeout) instead of spawning it unbounded, since add_with_weight_and_github_push calls gh_probe from inside the tasks-file lock's critical section and a hung gh could otherwise hold that lock indefinitely and block every other session's backlog add/next --claim; a timeout now fails soft to local-only, same as gh being absent. v0.2.6 makes is_github_remote compare the parsed host exactly against github.com instead of a substring match, so lookalike hosts (github.company.internal, github.com.evil.example) or a github.com occurrence in the path/query of a different host no longer false-positive as a GitHub remote. v0.2.5 wires the fail-soft one-way GitHub-issue push end to end: `backlog add` against a github.com-remote project now calls `gh issue create` (via an injected runner, mirroring condukt::pr) inside the same tasks-file-lock critical section as the add, and on success persists issue_number/issue_url on the new Task; a non-GitHub remote, absent gh, or a failed gh invocation all fail-soft to the pre-existing local-only add. v0.2.4 adds issue_number/issue_url (Option, serde default) fields to Task to hold a linked GitHub issue reference; backward-compatible with existing tasks.toml records. v0.2.3 adds a GitHub issue-create helper module (github.rs). v0.2.2 changes `backlog list`'s default scope to the cwd-resolved project (matching what `add --project "$PWD"` would have stored) instead of cross-project; pass `--all` to keep the old cross-project default (an explicit `--project` still wins over both). v0.1.14 closes a project-key normalization gap in harness_core::discovery::resolve_repo_root's last-resort fallback (used by canonicalize_project for --project values): when a path is not a git repo (or git is absent) AND fs::canonicalize fails because the path doesn't exist locally (e.g. written by a different machine/worktree), the fallback previously returned the raw, unresolved cwd verbatim -- no `.`/`..` collapsing, no trailing-slash stripping -- so `/foo/bar/`, `/foo/./bar`, and `/foo/baz/../bar` could each resolve to a DIFFERENT key for the SAME logical path, silently fragmenting one project's tasks/records across multiple stores. A new filesystem-independent `lexical_normalize` (Path::components()-based, no canonicalize/stat) is now the final fallback so the same logical path always collapses to the same key. v0.1.13 fails the next_claim read-modify-write CLOSED when the tasks-file lock cannot be acquired: with_tasks_lock ran its closure UNPROTECTED on a degraded acquire (contention/FS error), so concurrent next_claim callers could read the same pending task and mark it claimed in each -- dispatching ONE task to multiple processes. A new with_tasks_lock_aware tells the claim RMW whether the exclusive lock is actually held; when it is not, the claim now DECLINES (returns no task) and retries on the next tick rather than racing. Best-effort mutators keep the fail-soft with_tasks_lock (lost-update at worst, not double-dispatch). Deterministic regression test via the locked seam. v0.1.12 fixes a real lost-update race in add_with_weight/next_claim under heavy concurrent contention: the tasks-file lock's retry budget was sized for one legitimate holder's worst-case hold (300ms), not N holders queuing serially, so heavy contention (10 adders + 10 claimers) could exceed the budget and force an unprotected fallback that lost updates; budget raised from ~2s to ~8s, proven by a previously-red stress test now green. v0.1.11 adds a regression test proving the v0.1.10 heartbeat_at+TTL fix works without waiting the real 30-minute TTL (rewrites on-disk heartbeat_at back past the TTL, then confirms `backlog lock heartbeat` refreshes/protects it and an un-heartbeated lock is correctly reaped). v0.1.10 fixes backlog::lock's cross-session mutual exclusion: staleness was judged by the recorded pid's liveness, but that pid is always the one-shot `backlog lock acquire` CLI's own pid (dead again the instant the command returns), so any lock could be immediately stolen by another session regardless of whether the holder was still active. Staleness is now judged by a `heartbeat_at` timestamp + 30-minute TTL (matching condukt's task-claim and overwatch's lease registries), with a new `backlog lock heartbeat` subcommand. Subscription-native (skill + hook + bundled Rust binary, no API key).

plugins.name: budgetguard
plugins.description: v0.1.16: verdict-path audit (docs/audit-budgetguard-verdict-paths.md) closed seven fail-open paths. A budgetguard.toml that exists but cannot be read or PARSED no longer degrades to Config::default() — whose all-zero limits mean 'no limit', so one TOML typo silently disarmed the gate (measured: verdict(999,999)==Allow); config loading is now tri-state and an unreadable config blocks. A ledger lock that could not be acquired no longer proceeds with an unserialized read-modify-write; the day total is reported unmeasured instead of as headroom. An unreadable lock file is no longer assumed stale and stolen from a live session. A genuinely ABSENT config still means 'configured nothing' and still allows. v0.1.13: new `emit_violation(root, session, check_kind)` records an `overwatch` `ViolationSource::Budgetguard` event when a Stop is blocked for exceeding session/daily budget, feeding the unified review-queue. Real-time cost budget gate for Claude Code: on Stop, read the session transcript, compute USD cost, and block the turn when session or daily limits are exceeded — feeding the overage back so the agent winds down gracefully. Subscription-native (one Stop hook + bundled Rust binary, no API key). v0.1.11: Stop hook now runs under harness-core's run_guarded panic barrier (fail-closed block on crash instead of silent allow).

plugins.name: compass
plugins.description: v0.1.15: cargo fmt --all reformatting only (fixes the 'build & commit plugin binaries' smoke workflow's `cargo fmt --all --check` gate, chronically red on main since 2026-07-21 per scripts/check-ci-red.py); no behavior change. Goal re-grounding + next-move derivation upstream of condukt for Claude Code: when the goal goes fuzzy or you stall after finishing a chunk, it carves the project charter (north star + definition of done + current gap) through an interrogate loop, then routes only the right-sized next move into condukt while parking side-quests to taskprog. v0.1.14 fixes a fail-open in gather.rs: a `.deepwiki/` directory that exists but cannot be read (permission denied) was silently treated as empty via `.flatten()`, indistinguishable from a genuinely-absent directory; gather() now fails closed (Err) on cannot-determine while still tolerating a legitimately-missing directory. v0.1.13 fixes the C2 freshness DoD-ref check (Signal 3): CJK prose glued directly (no whitespace) to an embedded path or fraction was misread as one bogus token, and a leading `.` was stripped from dotfile paths (`.githooks/pre-commit` read as the non-existent `githooks/pre-commit`) — both caused false 'charter stale' positives. v0.1.12 fixed a lost-update race in the shared discovery store (harness_core::discovery): a concurrent `select` (load->mutate->rewrite) could silently clobber a concurrent `record` append (or another `select`) landing mid-cycle; both now share an advisory lock, proven by a multi-process regression test. Subscription-native (SessionStart nudge + Stop breadcrumb hooks + /compass skill + bundled Rust binary, no API key).

plugins.name: condukt
plugins.description: v0.7.151 integrates this line with the remote's. From this line: `enforce_edit_gate` no longer resolves a malformed verdict to `Allow` — the `required` / `fallback` / `broken` fields are read three-valued and any one of them being unreadable is 判定不能, which resolves to `Reject` (CLAUDE.md 3); and `worktree reconcile`'s DEATH rule third clause moved off the cwd-dependent transcript slug onto the session registry. v0.7.144 integrates this machine's line. `worktree::remove` no longer force-discards uncommitted work: both `Known(true)` and `Undetermined` now bail and leave the directory on disk, and the test that had pinned the permissive behaviour as correct (`worktree_remove_force_removes_dirty_worktree`, asserting verbatim that a "dirty worktree should be force-removed") was replaced rather than kept green. A disinterested agent observed the RED first and a third agent's mutation killed 3/3. v0.7.143: v0.7.141 のスケジューラ側並列上限 (schedule のバッチ幅分割 / Config::load の clamp / consensus / adversarial) を revert し、強制を parallelguard (PreToolUse で in-flight を数えて deny) へ移した。あわせて origin/main を統合し、3rd taintguard trigger を撤去した v0.7.140 を取り込む — `condukt lessons record-retrieval` は `taintguard::state::mark` を呼ばず、`taintguard` path 依存も無い (crates/condukt/src/main.rs:2174 に理由のコメントだけが残る)。これは封じ込めの REMOVAL であって移設ではない: cross-project lesson injection は untrusted provenance として追跡されず、その後に write 系ツールを downgrade する gate も無い。`tests/lessons_taint_trigger.rs` は固定していた挙動ごと削除済み。 v0.7.141: 1 セッションの同時実行を 3 に上限化。max_parallel は doc 上「advisory」で実際には誰も強制しておらず、schedule はバッチ幅を切らないまま 5 タスクを 1 バッチ 5 並列にしていた。schedule_capped がバッチを cap で分割し (切るだけでタスクは落とさない partition)、Config::load が harness_core::parallel::cap_fanout で clamp するので config.toml も CONDUKT_MAX_PARALLEL も下げられるが上げられない。consensus samples と adversarial panel の上限 5 も同じ cap に従う (floor 2 は維持 = 1 サンプルの合議は測っていない同意を報告する fail-open なので cap より優先)。 v0.7.117: wires the 3rd taintguard trigger — "this turn consumed cross-project lessons" — into `condukt lessons record-retrieval`. On the same non-empty-hit condition the existing retrieval-ledger `hit` flag already uses, the handler now calls `taintguard::state::mark(&cwd, &run, "lessons")` (new `taintguard` path dependency, mirroring the existing `blastguard`/`overwatch` deps; taintguard itself is unchanged), tainting the session so taintguard's PreToolUse `gate` downgrades write-class tools for the rest of the turn — mirroring the existing web/external-read triggers. A zero-hit search stays a no-op (preserves the empty `lessons_context: []` contract); a failed `mark` is `eprintln!`'d and does not fail the command. New `tests/lessons_taint_trigger.rs` confirms RED (no taint) with the mark call disabled and GREEN once wired, plus an anti-vacuity zero-hit case and a regression on the unchanged retrieval-ledger/lessons_context shape. v0.7.113: PROGRESS-not-liveness gate on the cross-session claim reap (mirrors backlog's lock-reap fix) — `claim::reap` no longer evicts a heartbeat-stale claim on heartbeat-age alone (the fail-open that force-steals a live-but-quiet run: fresh commits / growing transcript / advancing tasks, heartbeat merely lapsed). A stale claim is now reaped ONLY when its owning run's PROGRESS is confirmed `Known(Stalled)` by the reusable `harness_core::progress` engine — git HEAD + the owning session's transcript + the run's max task `updated_at` frozen across the multi-sample window (default 90s, `HARNESS_PROGRESS_WINDOW_SECS`). Progressing OR Undetermined (unreadable signal / no prior sample / window not elapsed) NEVER reap (fail-closed). The run-progress signal is deliberately max(task.updated_at), NOT the run-state file mtime (heartbeats rewrite that file = liveness, not progress). All five reap call sites (claim_files/claim_tasks/heartbeat/active_claims/write_execution_state) thread the same progress probe. New `condukt state probe --run RID [--json]` reports, per RUNNING task, the durable signals, `last_progress_age_secs`, and the three-valued verdict — the observability twin sampling the same engine. Tests: the two stale-reap unit tests now encode the tighter contract (reap requires a forced `Known(Stalled)` via a `#[cfg(test)]` thread-local seam, compiled out of production); new protective tests pin the fail-closed half (Progressing / Undetermined ⇒ NOT reaped) observed RED against the old ungated reap; docstrings updated in the same commit. v0.7.109: closed an F→P oracle fail-open (backlog 22b69f6a) — `oracle::check_oracle`'s top-of-function exemption used to fire on `!requires_oracle || reproduction_tests.is_none()`, so a fix/feature task (`requires_oracle:true`) that simply did not DECLARE `reproduction_tests` was exempted from the Fail→Pass gate even when real tdd RED→GREEN proofs existed for it. Narrowed the guard to `!requires_oracle` alone: a fix/feature task is now ALWAYS consulted against `tdd` regardless of whether it declared `reproduction_tests` (missing declarations degrade to the tdd `unknown`/spawn-Err paths, never a free pass). The `reproduction_tests` param is retained for call-site signature stability (renamed `_reproduction_tests`) but is no longer a gate switch; the doc comment and the exempt `reason` string (`"not a fix/feature task"`, no longer `"or no reproduction_tests"`) were updated in the same commit to match. The tdd-spawn and spawn-Err (`"a missing checker is not a passing checker"`) branches are unchanged. v0.7.108: added a must-ask-human / untestable clamp to the graded-autonomy policy (backlog 903a0d28) — new `policy::decide_untestable(risk, reversibility, confidence)` mirrors `decide_conflict_resolution`: it calls `decide` and clamps an `Auto` verdict up to `Escalate`, passing `Escalate`/`Block` through unchanged (pure, total, no opt-in path back to Auto), so CLAUDE.md §2's "if a thing cannot be meaningfully tested, ask the human" gate can never be auto-self-answered. Wired a `--untestable` bool flag into both `policy decide` and `policy answer` (mirrors `--conflict`); when set, the verdict is computed by `decide_untestable`, so an otherwise-`auto` untestable decision falls through to a real AskUserQuestion (exit 2, `{"answered":false,"policy":"escalate"}`, never journaled). `--untestable` takes precedence over `--conflict` (both clamp Auto→Escalate identically). Backward-compatible: an empty precedent store renders a byte-identical brief to today. v0.7.46: new `review-worthiness` subcommand — a deterministic review-WORTHINESS (review-COST) score, distinct from blastguard/diffrisk's blast-radius, summing four bounded penalty terms (size scaled by total changed lines, net-deletion, missing-rationale, absent-task-link) into a `score` + human-readable `drivers`; primary flag mode is hermetic (no git), an optional fail-soft `--from-git` convenience mode gathers numstat/log signals from a live repo. Kept fully separate from `review-brief`'s no-live-diff purity contract; feeds a future review-budget allocator. v0.7.47: new `review-order` subcommand — a deterministic review-ORDER pass that reorders a diff's hunks so a human reviews top-to-bottom: a fresh unified-diff hunk parser plus a pure edge-builder/orderer clusters logically-connected hunks (union-find weakly-connected components) and topologically sorts each cluster (Kahn's algorithm, deterministic min-key tiebreak/cycle-break) so definitions come before the hunks that reference them, reusing blastguard's caller-enumeration and harness-core's symbol extraction as the reference/definition source; `--diff-file` is the hermetic tested contract, `--from-git` a fail-soft convenience.

plugins.name: context-governor
plugins.description: A thin control layer around Claude Code's built-in compaction: pin + lossless-recall + retrieval + tool-hygiene, wired as a single hook-dispatch binary. Separates the three axes it touches — size (window occupancy), cost (recompute/cache), correctness (norm preservation) — and never writes its own lossy summarizer (compression is delegated to built-in compaction). Subscription-native (hooks + binary, no API key).

plugins.name: ctxrot
plugins.description: v0.5.22: new `ctxrot handoff-record` (PostToolUse:Read) / `ctxrot handoff` (PreToolUse:Task) hooks address one measured pattern from real session transcripts — a parent session Reads a large file, then dispatches a Task/subagent whose prompt concerns that same file, and the subagent pays for a redundant fresh Read of content the parent already has. handoff-record caches a Read's content (session_id + resolved absolute path + content, capped per-entry, bounded ring buffer on disk) once it clears a size floor; handoff matches a dispatching Task's prompt against that session's cached paths (substring match only — never a bare filename, and never across sessions, since there is no sibling-to-sibling correlation id in the hook payload) and splices the cached content into the prompt via `hookSpecificOutput.updatedInput`, so the subagent's first Read becomes unnecessary. This does NOT reduce total resident tokens system-wide — the content still occupies the subagent's context exactly once either way — it only avoids the wasted round trip and a subagent walking into preguard's size gate with no recourse; docs are explicit that this is not a token-count win. True concurrent sibling-subagent deduplication was investigated and found structurally infeasible via Claude Code's current hook API (confirmed: no parent_tool_use_id/batch-correlation field exists in PreToolUse/PostToolUse payloads) and was deliberately NOT attempted. bin/ctxrot (the POSIX launcher)'s missing-binary fallback gained the two new subcommands to its non-verdict exit-0 branch (they were previously absent and would have fallen through to the CLI-command `exit 1` default, which would have broken PreToolUse:Task on a host with no bundled binary); tests/launcher_missing_binary.rs's observability-hooks test now covers both. v0.5.21: `bin/ctxrot` (the POSIX launcher) no longer maps a MISSING per-platform binary to a blanket silent `exit 0`. A missing build means the check did not run, and exit-0-with-no-output is byte-identical to a clean run, so every verdict-bearing subcommand silently read as "nothing to flag": preguard granted the load gate, toolguard let an unmeasured payload through, stop ended the turn as if the budget check had passed, and statusline rendered the blank bar that reads as headroom (the 3b1eb24 fail-open). Each now resolves the cannot-determine on the restrictive side of its OWN protocol — preguard emits `permissionDecision: ask` (a refusal to guess; a `deny` would be unescapable for every Read/Bash), toolguard emits an `additionalContext` UNMEASURED marker, stop emits `{"decision":"block"}` bounded by `stop_hook_active` exactly like harness_core::gate::run's panic barrier (empty stdin = a manual run: exit 1, no fabricated decision), and statusline prints the explicit `unknown` band. The CLI/skill-consumed subcommands (note/metrics/ctx/usage/eval/…), whose empty stdout would be read as real data ("no notes", "nothing dropped"), now exit 1 like bin/evalkit. Only the pure-observability hooks (guard/rescue/restore/distill-bg — conditional prose injected into context, no machine consumer) keep exit 0, and they still report on stderr; README.ja.md gains the launcher classification table enumerating each subcommand's downstream consumers (CLAUDE.md §1's requirement for any module claiming the non-verdict carve-out) and states the residual limit that hook stderr is only visible in debug output. src/main.rs's stale "on any error we exit 0 and stay silent" module docstring was corrected to match the code. New tests/launcher_missing_binary.rs pins every row of that table, plus that a PRESENT binary is still exec'd with args passed through. v0.5.18: `hooks::stop::run()` now returns `(json, check_kind: &'static str)`; `stop_run` records an `overwatch` `ViolationSource::Ctxrot` event via a new `emit_violation(root, session, check_kind)` (observed check_kind values: `unmeasurable-transcript`, `budget-threshold-crossed`), feeding the unified review-queue. v0.5.16: cargo fmt --all reformatting only (fixes the 'build & commit plugin binaries' smoke workflow's `cargo fmt --all --check` gate, chronically red on main since 2026-07-21 per scripts/check-ci-red.py); no behavior change. Context-rot guard for Claude Code: detect, rescue, restore, distill, and CONTROL what loads into context (rule-based allow/deny gate + /ctx pin/drop/load + switchable carryover). Subscription-native (hooks + subagent + skill, no API key). v0.5.15: `usage::find_transcript_for_session`'s `~/.claude/projects` scan no longer swallows a permission-denied (or other non-NotFound) read_dir/entry error into the same silent `None` as a legitimately-absent directory — the non-NotFound case now also surfaces via `eprintln!`; the `None` → "unknown" readout callers already render is unchanged (an absent dir was never a fail-open here, since the caller already treats `None` as cannot-determine). New regression tests cover an absent projects dir and a chmod-000 unreadable one. v0.5.14: the Stop hook now runs under harness-core's `run_guarded` panic barrier — a panic in `stop_run` fails CLOSED (`decision:block`) instead of the old `run_hook` behavior of silently exiting 0 with no decision. v0.5.12: the Stop-hook compact nudge now fails CLOSED on a cannot-determine reading — when `estimate_tokens` falls back to the cache-blind bytes proxy (no `usage` block parsed) yet that proxy, a LOWER bound on true usage, has already reached band 1, the hook surfaces a one-shot `/compact` nudge instead of silently allowing a possibly-over-budget session to keep growing; previously its high 0.90 block threshold let a truncated/corrupt transcript read low and never nudge (behavioral twin of the v0.5.10/v0.5.11 render fixes). Bounded to fire ONCE per session (dedicated `.compact-unmeasured` sentinel, never a turn-trap); a genuine early session below band 1 stays silent (no over-alarm) and the eventual genuine over-threshold reading still blocks. v0.5.11: the context-usage readout (statusline + `ctxrot usage`) no longer renders a bytes-proxy estimate as a confident band — `estimate_tokens`'s source (`"bytes"` = a rough size/4 guess with no real usage block, vs `"usage"` = authoritative) is threaded through `usage::line` instead of discarded, so an estimate carries an `est?` marker and, when it lands in the green band, is DIMMED (neutral, not confident green) so a truncated/corrupt transcript reading low can't read as "plenty of headroom"; a high estimate keeps its alarming color and authoritative readings are unchanged. v0.5.10: the `statusline` render now fails CLOSED on a cannot-determine — a non-empty-but-unparseable payload, or a transcript that can't be read/estimated, renders an explicit non-green `?% … unknown` band (mirroring `ctxrot usage`'s "不明") instead of printing nothing; a blank status bar silently read as "plenty of headroom" (fail-open twin of the already-hardened Stop-hook path). Empty stdin / no session still renders blank; exit stays 0 so the bar never crashes. v0.5.9: the preguard (PreToolUse) and toolguard (PostToolUse) hooks now wrap their detectors in a `std::panic::catch_unwind` barrier (`analyse`) — a panic in the analysis maps to a deny (preguard) or a fail-closed placeholder+nudge (toolguard) instead of the un-analysed call/output silently passing through, closing a fail-open (blastguard 同型). v0.5.8: `guard::fetch_session_lease`'s `overwatch lease` subprocess call is now bounded by an 8s timeout (wait_timeout, kill+reap on expiry) instead of a plain unbounded `Command::output()`, so a hung overwatch binary can no longer wedge the UserPromptSubmit hook; the spawn/timeout/kill mechanics are split into a testable `run_with_timeout` helper.

plugins.name: curate
plugins.description: Promote fugu-router playbooks into versioned golden eval datasets for evalkit: turn the append-only routing log into a curated, deduplicated holdout set. Mechanical acceptance criteria (`cargo test`, a backticked command) become runnable golden cases; the rest become drafts for a human to fill. The supply side of the offline eval loop. Subscription-native (one bundled Rust binary, no API key).

plugins.name: deepwiki
plugins.description: v0.1.5: cargo fmt --all reformatting only (fixes the 'build & commit plugin binaries' smoke workflow's `cargo fmt --all --check` gate, chronically red on main since 2026-07-21 per scripts/check-ci-red.py); no behavior change. Repository architecture wiki for Claude Code: a /deepwiki command that maps the repo with a bundled Rust scanner, has a subagent write & refresh hierarchical wiki pages (.deepwiki/*.md) with source links, and tracks freshness against git. Inspired by Devin Wiki. Subscription-native (binary + subagent + command, no API key). v0.1.4: `scan.rs`'s three readdir walks (`scan`'s top-level summary, `walk`, `count_files`) no longer swallow an unreadable subdirectory or entry via `.flatten()`/`let-else` into the same silent skip as a legitimately-vanished one — a non-NotFound error now surfaces via `eprintln!` while the scan still degrades to whatever was readable (this is a best-effort repo-map generator feeding a wiki-writer subagent, not a gate, so partial results remain correct behavior — only the silent swallowing of a real permission error was the bug). New regression test scans a tree with a chmod-000 subdirectory and confirms the readable files are still counted.

plugins.name: difflog
plugins.description: Session diff-log for Claude Code: snapshot HEAD at SessionStart, write a structured git diff summary (commits, stat, files changed, bounded diff body) at SessionEnd. A /difflog skill can generate a human-readable narrative from the log. Subscription-native (no API key). v0.1.5: `list`/`last`'s shared `md_entries` helper no longer swallows an unreadable individual directory entry via `.filter_map(|e| e.ok())`, and distinguishes a missing `log_dir` ("not found") from an existing-but-unreadable one ("unreadable", now surfaced) instead of both silently reading as "no logs". New regression tests cover an absent dir, a chmod-000 unreadable dir, and md-only filtering.

plugins.name: ship
plugins.description: v0.1.9: cargo fmt --all reformatting only (fixes the 'build & commit plugin binaries' smoke workflow's `cargo fmt --all --check` gate, chronically red on main since 2026-07-21 per scripts/check-ci-red.py); no behavior change. Shipping-ritual nudge for Claude Code: deterministically detect unshipped state (uncommitted changes, unmerged condukt/* branches, leftover worktrees, unpushed commits, stale plugin binaries) and remind you to commit・merge・push・rebuild・rollout. A /ship skill and a fail-soft SessionEnd hook surface the checklist; only the plugin-rebuild (`--run-safe`, now `--stage-repo` so it refreshes the committed binary that stale-detection measures) and plugin-rollout (`ship rollout`, automates `/plugin update`) steps are auto-runnable — commit/merge/push stay human-gated. Subscription-native (no API key).

plugins.name: donegate
plugins.description: v0.1.30 integrates this line with the remote's: the session-scoped skip now carries a third state. Session-scoping fixed WHOSE token is consumed; it did not fix WHEN. A Stop is adjudicated by four independent gate processes, so a token honoured by one that allows was burned even when another blocked the same stop — the stop never happened and the one-shot escape had been spent on nothing, which is standing pressure toward a permanent bypass (CLAUDE.md 5). `consume_session_skip` now takes `stop_hook_active` and parks an honoured token as `<id>.skip.honoured`: it is re-honoured while a re-entry after a block is in flight, and deleted the first time a chain actually ends. A rename failure that can neither bound nor clear the token is resolved to NOT honouring it. v0.1.28: the shared project-root `.donegate-skip` marker is gone. The operator escape is now `donegate skip --reason "..."`, which is scoped to the issuing session (CLAUDE.md 5 forbids a shared one-shot file under parallel sessions, since whichever session stops next consumes it), requires a non-empty reason, and appends both the issue and the consumption to the gate log so a bypass cannot happen unrecorded. v0.1.26: leaves a durable sentinel when the attempt cap is exhausted (a give-up is recorded under its own `giveup:<name>` signature so it can never share a signature with an enforced block), adds a behavioural test for the record-failure visibility path, and CORRECTS prose that claimed one session's repeated give-ups surface in `overwatch review-queue`. Measured false: donegate passes the session key as BOTH `task_key` and `session_id`, so `is_systemic` (which needs distinct_tasks>1 or sessions>1) can never fire for a single session -- three give-ups still yielded `[]`. v0.1.24: an UNTRUSTED project that declares checks now BLOCKS the stop instead of rendering as `checks: 0` (which allowed every stop) - a refusal to judge is no longer emitted as a clean verdict; config resolution returns a four-valued `Declaration` (Absent / Loaded / RefusedUntrusted / Unreadable), an unreadable-or-unparseable config blocks too, and trust now inherits across the one linked-worktree-to-main-working-tree hop so session worktrees of a trusted repo are trusted. v0.1.21: re-bless the verdict compile-fail trybuild golden stderr again — CI's `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable` has no `rust-src` component, which changes how rustc renders `note:` snippets pointing into std/core; a local toolchain with rust-src installed produces the longer form and silently re-diverges the golden. Reproduced against a `--profile minimal` toolchain matching CI exactly. No contract change. v0.1.20: re-bless the verdict compile-fail trybuild golden stderr again (rustc now emits additional note-body lines for E0599; the compile-fail invariant is unchanged, same category of drift as v0.1.18). v0.1.18: re-bless the verdict trybuild .stderr (removed stale std-lib note bodies that a newer rustc no longer renders; the compile-fail invariant is unchanged). v0.1.17: new `emit_violations(root, session, failing: &[String])` records one `overwatch` `ViolationSource::Donegate` event per failing check name (fmt/clippy/test) after `gate_run` blocks a Stop, feeding the unified review-queue. Completion-verification gate for Claude Code: on Stop, run your acceptance commands as subprocesses and block the stop until every required check is green, feeding failures back for an auto-fix loop. Subscription-native (one hook + bundled Rust binary, no API key). v0.1.8: added #![deny(clippy::panic)] at crate root.

plugins.name: evalkit
plugins.description: Offline golden-regression eval harness for Claude Code plugins: read golden *.jsonl cases (file-content or CLI-output assertions) and exit non-zero when a prompt edit or CLI contract regresses. The offline sibling of condukt's online verifier — runnable as a CI gate with no API key. Subscription-native (one bundled Rust binary).

plugins.name: benchkit
plugins.description: v0.1.8: `auditsample.rs`'s `gate_name()` match arm now covers the 6 new `ViolationSource` variants (Donegate/Reviewgate/Tdd/Budgetguard/Autoflow/Ctxrot) added to overwatch's cross-gate ledger; no behavior change to sampling logic. External-benchmark (SWE-bench Verified) runner for Claude Code plugins: a typed SWE-bench Instance model, a deterministic fixture-based JSONL loader, and a gated `download` subcommand that shells out to `curl` (no HTTP crate) to fetch the Princeton NLP dataset only on explicit invocation. Subscription-native (one bundled Rust binary).

plugins.name: flow
plugins.description: v0.2.11: spec-gap を4番目の source として足した (Step 3-1.5、specs/spec-loop.toml R4-flow-spec-gap-source)。正典が無いと分かった課題を condukt の実装フェーズへ盲目投入せず specforge へ差し戻し、draft -> ratify が通れば要件が backlog に積まれて次の周回で拾われる。trigger は3つ (condukt interpreter の open_questions / task の confidence:low / specguard brief の verdict=not-covered)。判定不能 (brief の undetermined・binary 不在・出力が読めない) は divert を起こさず人間へ surface する — not-covered は specforge に新しい spec を書かせる書き込み側の動作なので、判定不能をそこへ丸めると「読めなかった」が「仕様が無い」に化ける (CLAUDE.md 第3節)。divert の可否は condukt policy answer を --approval なしで通し (判断要求なので escalate)、gate-decisions.jsonl に残る。divert 回数を数えるカウンタは足していない — 停止は R0 の ratify contract floor で決まる (09148819 の notes が 2026-07-31 にカウンタ案を RETRACT 済み)。 v0.2.10: v0.2.8 のバッチ幅ハードルールを revert した (同時実行の強制は parallelguard が PreToolUse で行う)。旧文: claim するバッチ幅 N の既定を 4 から 3 に下げ、3 が上限 (1 セッションあたりの同時実行上限) であることをハードルールに明記。並列 or 直列の実判定は従来どおり condukt の schedule が決定論的に行う。あわせて origin/main を統合し、SKILL.md の「実際に流れを止めるのは deterministic gate の側である」の列挙から taintguard (2026-08-24 にユーザー裁定で repo から撤去) を外した版を取り込む — 今は blastguard / donegate / pre-commit・pre-push hook を名指しする (crates/flow/skills/flow/SKILL.md:140)。 Unified source→executor driver for Claude Code: a /flow skill that binds the task SOURCES (compass next-move + backlog queue) to the EXECUTOR (condukt, model-routed by fugu-router) in one HOTL loop — gate on compass freshness, pick the highest-priority task, hand it to condukt, verify, mark done, repeat. v0.2.7 RETIRES the SessionStart proposal on the user's instruction: through 0.2.6 a `flow propose` hook injected an L2 propose-then-confirm directive every session the backlog had pending items ("before starting other work, ask with a single AskUserQuestion whether to start /flow"), and autoflow said the same thing twice more — its own SessionStart proposal and a Stop-hook arm that BLOCKED every turn with "/backlog を実行してください". Two plugins were making one request, one of them on every turn, and repetition is not detection: the tenth "there are N items" carries no information the first did not. Whether to drain the queue is the operator's call and typing /flow IS that call, so the hook, the launcher, the binary and the Cargo package are all gone — `propose` was the binary's only subcommand, so nothing was left for it to do. flow is now a SKILLS-ONLY plugin (the shape scout and daily-report already ship). The /flow skill itself is unchanged except for the lines that claimed it would be proposed automatically; it now says explicitly that the agent must NOT propose /flow on its own, because reconstructing the retired directive by hand would undo the retirement. The one test worth keeping moved rather than being deleted with the package: `skill_queue_contract.rs` reads SKILL.md as text and now lives at crates/integration-tests/tests/flow_skill_queue_contract.rs, still pinning that the loop does not take the exclusive project lock and that the pick reserves a task instead of only reading it. Subscription-native (skill only, no binary, no API key).

plugins.name: fugu-router
plugins.description: v0.1.28: fixes the defect v0.1.27's wiring fix exposed — the hook was reachable again, but `sync` could not finish from the store's own steady state. `cmd_sync` pulled BEFORE committing local appends, and pulled with `--ff-only`; both abort in normal operation (uncommitted appends make `git pull` refuse with "local changes would be overwritten", exit 1; a second machine's push makes `--ff-only` exit 128). Order is now commit → pull `--no-rebase --no-edit` → push. Because two machines appending to the same JSONL conflict on adjacent end-of-file additions, `sync` also ensures the sync dir's `.gitattributes` declares `episodes.jsonl`/`playbooks.jsonl` as `merge=union` (keeps both sides' lines; the store dedups by content hash, so a duplicate is recoverable where a dropped episode is not). A failed sync no longer fails into silence: it is written to `~/.fugu-router/sync-error.json` and surfaced by the `UserPromptSubmit` hook as both `additionalContext` and `systemMessage` until a later sync clears it. New test `sync_ordering.rs` (4 tests, RED before GREEN). v0.1.27: `hooks/hooks.json` now declares the record-store sync as a `SessionEnd` hook (`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/fugu-router sync`, timeout 30). The wiring previously existed only as an orphaned absolute path in the user's `~/.claude/settings.json` (`~/.cargo/bin/fugu-router sync`), whose build had been renamed away — so the hook exited 127 every session with neither exit code nor stderr reaching the agent or the user, making a sync that had nothing to do indistinguishable from a sync that never ran (it went dark, not red). Measured 2026-08-26: the last `fugu-router sync` commit in `~/.fugu-router/record-repo` is 2026-07-23 09:57:38 +0900, while `episodes.jsonl`/`playbooks.jsonl` there kept growing as uncommitted, unpushed working-tree modifications for ~34 days. New test `session_end_sync_hook_wired.rs` requires the declaration to live in-plugin, every declared command to resolve through `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` and never `~/.cargo/bin`, and every declared subcommand to exist in the binary. v0.1.25: `Episode.duration_secs` is now tri-state (`Option<f64>`) — an absent field OR a legacy on-disk `0.0` both deserialize to `None` ("unmeasured"), never conflated with a genuine measured zero, via a custom `de_duration_secs` deserializer; a new writer omits the field entirely when unmeasured (`skip_serializing_if`). `record --duration` is now `Option<f64>`: a non-positive value (0 or negative) is an explicit error + non-zero exit ("omit --duration to record the episode as unmeasured"), never silently stored. `stats` and `duration`/`duration-outliers` surface a duration-coverage count (`measured_n/total_n`, plus `duration_coverage` in `--json`) so the fraction of episodes with a real measurement is visible instead of a silent 0.0-average dilution; `duration-outliers` and `delegation-stats` now average only measured episodes. RED→GREEN recorded via tdd --task t3. v0.1.24: new mode axis `--mode fast|normal|high` for `route`/`suggest` — a deterministic clamp applied AFTER the policy has already picked a worker/verifier pair (never touches `decide`/`decide_bandit`'s learning logic). `fast` shifts the worker one tier down (capped at sonnet — opus never selected as worker or verifier); `high` shifts one tier up (capped at opus); `normal` is the backward-compatible identity default. The verifier is always recomputed from the clamped worker via `policy::verifier_model`, additionally capped at sonnet under `fast`. Precedence: `--mode` flag > env `FUGU_ROUTER_MODE` > config.toml `mode` > `normal`; an invalid env/config value is an explicit error + non-zero exit, never silently coerced to `normal`. A `gated` decision is a no-op under every mode. Ordering: the mode clamp runs BEFORE `downgrade_for_budget` — budget wins over a mode preference, and the rationale records both the mode's shift and any budget negation so a `high` pick never silently disappears. `Episode` gains a measurement-only `mode: Option<String>` field (`record --mode`); an absent value means "not recorded", never conflated with `Some("normal")`. v0.1.22: `fingerprint::collect_skills`'s SKILL.md corpus walk no longer silently skips an unreadable directory/entry/file the same way it skips a legitimately-absent one — since this module exists specifically to detect a silent skill edit, a SKILL.md that becomes unreadable defeating that detection is now surfaced via `eprintln!` while the walk still degrades to whatever was readable (fail-soft, unchanged contract). New regression test: a chmod-000 subdirectory doesn't panic and the still-readable sibling SKILL.md is still hashed. v0.1.20: new `duration-outliers [--json] [--threshold <x>]` command flags models whose avg duration within a task class is a relative outlier vs other models in the same class (default threshold 1.5x the cross-model mean), and cross-references outlier-vs-normal effective pass rate — the measurement tool built to test PDO hypothesis ae64db03. v0.1.19: `Episode` gains measurement-only `route_basis`/`route_confidence`/`route_rationale` (the routing `Decision`'s provenance), `lines_added`/`lines_removed`, and `tokens_input`/`tokens_output`, all `Option<_>` and backward-compatible; `record` gains matching `--route-basis`/`--route-confidence`/`--route-rationale`/`--lines-added`/`--lines-removed`/`--tokens-input`/`--tokens-output` flags. Not consulted by `policy::route`/`decide_bandit` — exists so routing decisions and task cost can be retrospectively correlated against actual pass/fail outcomes. fugu-style per-model routing for Claude Code orchestration. Learns from past task outcomes (which model passed verification, at what cost) and picks the cheapest Claude tier that historically clears similar work. Feeds condukt's suggested_model deterministically; records outcomes back to a local episode store. No API key, no embedding service — lexical k-NN over a JSONL store. v0.1.13: every git subprocess in `cmd_sync` (pull/clone/status/add/diff/commit/push) is now bounded by a timeout (30s network ops, 10s local ops) via `wait-timeout`, killing a hung/stalled git process instead of wedging the sync command indefinitely. v0.1.12: `store::append_playbook` now writes body+newline in one `write_all` call (mirroring `append`'s existing single-syscall pattern) instead of `writeln!`'s two syscalls, closing the same O_APPEND interleaving hazard for playbook records; a JSON-serialization failure now propagates as an `io::Result` error instead of silently writing an empty line. plugins.description: v0.1.24 integrates this line with the remote's. plugins.name: specguard
plugins.description: v0.2.56: `scope::code_index_files` はもう `fugu-router` を spawn しない。`harness_core::index_store` を同一プロセスで呼ぶ（1 クエリあたり 2 プロセス起動と JSON round trip が消滅）。加えて symbol 索引だけでなく**全文索引**も引くので、宣言行ではなく本文にしか現れない名前 — つまり呼び出し箇所 — でファイルが relevant-file map に載るようになった（旧 `fugu-router code-index search` は 宣言行しか見ていないので構造的に不可能だった）。判定不能は空ではなく `Undetermined`（CLAUDE.md 3: 「探せなかった」を「無かった」と同じ出力に写さない）。`MapEntry` に `symbols` / `called_by` / `ambiguous_symbols` を追加（`#[serde(default)]` で旧マップと後方互換）し、`map enrich` が決定論的索引から埋める。`called_by` は同名宣言が 4 ファイル以上ある symbol を辿らず、辿らなかった名前を `ambiguous_symbols` に**明記**する — 空の `called_by` が「誰も呼んでいない」と「辿れなかった」の 2 つを意味できてしまう状態を潰すため。新 CLI: `map search`（全文＋symbol の hit を map entry に帰属）/ `map callers`（永続化 call graph）/ `map enrich`。索引が答えられないとき `map` クエリは exit 10 で理由を stderr に出す — 0 件ヒットと同じ終了コードにしない。 v0.2.55: brief --json が三値 verdict (covered/not-covered/undetermined) を exit code 込みで返す (R3)。--json と --prompt は排他。 v0.2.54: specforge に専用 launcher (crates/specguard/bin/specforge) を追加し、rollout で実際に配布されるようにした。specforge は spec-loop R4 で /flow が spec gap を divert する先＝判定経路上にあるため、バイナリ不在時は sibling の specguard launcher と違って exit 0 せず非 0 で終了する (fail-closed。「spec を検査していない」が「spec gap は無い」と読まれない)。併せて scripts/rebuild-plugins.sh の seed ループが 1 plugin あたり glob 順で最初の launcher だけを seed して break していた不具合を修正した — 2 本目以降の launcher はバイナリが置かれないまま配布され DARK (インストール済み・版整合・何も実行しない・hook が起動しないので finding も出ない) になる。specguard の場合、先に並ぶのは specforge なので、落ちる側は GATE hook である specguard 本体だった。scripts/tests/rebuild-seeds-every-launcher.sh が F->P で pin する。 v0.2.53: v0.2.52 の「最大 3 体ずつの波に分ける」散文を revert した。散文は強制ではなく、同時実行数の上限は parallelguard が PreToolUse で deny して強制する。 v0.2.48: specforge ratify now has an EXIT to the queue — it files one backlog item per requirement of the spec it just ratified (src/forge/queue.rs, DESIGN.md §5.4). Before this a ratified spec had no implemented path into the queue at all; the only spec→backlog handoff was prose telling a human to run `backlog add` by hand, so specforge could produce canon but not work. Each item carries the spec id, the requirement id, and the requirement's acceptance criteria VERBATIM as its done_criteria block, so condukt's interpreter lifts them instead of re-deriving them from the statement (re-derivation is where a requirement quietly loses its teeth). Idempotent via a `req:<spec id>:<req id>` identity tag derived from the two ids alone: re-ratifying adds zero, editing a statement does not orphan its item into a duplicate, and another spec's R0 does not collide with this one's. The listing passes no --status filter on purpose (measured: `backlog list` still returns done tasks), so a COMPLETED requirement keeps suppressing its own re-queue rather than being resurrected. Cannot-determine does not guess (CLAUDE.md §3): a missing `backlog` binary, a non-zero exit, or an unparseable listing resolves to neither "queue is empty" (which duplicates everything) nor "already queued" (which silently discards what a human ratified) — it exits 9 (EXIT_QUEUE_FAILED) with the ratification intact, and `specforge queue --id <id>` retries the handoff alone. `specforge queue` refuses an unratified spec with exit 6 (the queue is downstream of consent) and `ratify --no-queue` makes opting out explicit rather than silent. v0.2.36: closed fail-open #7 (61599e06) — an audit whose marker was present but whose `needs_user` verdict was absent/empty/unrecognised was parsed as `no`/clean, advancing the baseline over content whose verdict was never established. parse.rs now fails closed with an asymmetric rule: the SURFACE side is liberal (a `yes`-prefixed token is a finding) but the CLEAN side is strict — only the bare token `no` clears the audit (the old `starts_with("no")` also cleared "not sure"/"no idea"/"not comparable", natural cannot-determine phrasings). Anything else is a first-class `indeterminate` state → needs_user=true that stays STICKY through the verify/refute pass (a skeptic can't drop it back to clean). All three audit prompts (audit/decisions/completeness) fixed in lockstep to instruct the auditor to emit `yes` (not `no`) when it cannot compare, and to emit exactly `yes` or `no`. 仕様↔実装 整合監査ハーネスを Claude Code から subscription-native に実行する。各 shard を read-only な in-session subagent で監査し (nested claude --print なし)、決定的ハーネス (scope/render/parse/report) は specguard バイナリに委譲する。

plugins.name: stuckguard
plugins.description: v0.1.30: `anchor::fetch_session_anchor`（PDO heartbeat piggyback §4.6b の唯一の経路）が判定不能（overwatch バイナリが解決できない／実行できない／出力をパースできない）を「lease 無し」と同じ silent `None` に潰していたのを是正した（backlog 1469673b、直前の `32ead775` で保留していた懸念が実在すると確定：overwatch の起動が LEASE_TTL_SECS=30分以上失敗し続けると生存中セッションの lease が黙って reap される）。`AnchorLookup`（Leased/NoLease/Undetermined）の三値で呼び出し側 (`main::watch`) の効果（advisory hook なので block しない）は変えず、判定不能のときだけ `stderr` に診断（セッションID・理由・heartbeat が飛んだ事実）を出す。overwatch バイナリ解決も `crates/ctxrot` の `find_overwatch_binary`（`std::fs::read_dir(&base).ok()?.filter_map(|e| e.ok())` で読めないキャッシュディレクトリを「候補ゼロ」に畳んでいた）を模倣せず、`harness_core::boundary::read_dir_entries` 経由にして不在（Known(空)）と判定不能（Undetermined）を区別する。config.rs の `describe_unreadable_config`/`load_with_diagnostics` と同じ流儀（純関数＋注入可能シンク）で実装し、本番経路（実バイナリの stderr）まで守るテストを追加。 v0.1.25: verdict-monotonicity の proptest を追加した（backlog a7d41587、テストのみ・production の挙動は不変）。永続化されたセッション履歴を truncate / corrupt / empty / chmod 000 しても「詰まっていない」へ倒れないことを性質として固定する。この経路は既に fail-closed（`main::watch` は Undetermined な load を nudge に解決する）なので修正ではなく ratchet であり、将来 `SessionState::default()` を静かに戻す編集をその編集について書かれていないテストが捕まえる。通ること自体は証拠にならないので、fail-closed 側を剥がした版を同一ファイル内に置いて性質が実際に落ちることを示す mutation テストと、4 種の degradation が全て実際に効いていることを確認する coverage テストを併置した（no-op になった degradation が黙って skip され続けるのを防ぐ）。 Stuck-loop detector + escalation for Claude Code: a PostToolUse hook that spots repeated identical actions and edit thrash, then injects an escalating nudge to change approach or ask the user for help. Subscription-native (one hook + bundled Rust binary, no API key).

plugins.name: autoflow
plugins.description: v0.1.23 is the integration point where this machine's line merges origin/main (e018fe91). It carries no behaviour change of its own: autoflow's code here is the remote's v0.1.22 retirement verbatim, and the number moves only because both merge parents had already published 0.1.22 for different trees, so leaving it in place would strand this tree behind a version nobody can distinguish. v0.1.22 RETIRES the backlog nudges on the user's instruction. Three paths asked the operator to work the queue and two of them are gone: the SessionStart hook that injected "バックログに {n} 件 (最優先: '{title}')。/flow で開始しますか？" (and "/compass で再接地して から /flow を実行してください" when the charter was stale), and the Stop-hook arm that, once the condukt pending set emptied, read the queue and BLOCKED the stop with "残課題バック ログに {n} 件…/backlog を実行してください" — every turn, until the queue emptied — behind a compass-freshness gate that existed only to guard that auto-driving. The condukt arm stays: an in-flight run this session started and abandoned is an accident, while a queue item nobody has started is not, and asking about it every turn adds no information. Repetition is not detection. What went with them, so nothing is left half-wired: the `session-start` subcommand and its hooks.json entry, the launcher's `session-start` arm (the arg now falls through to the catch-all `exit 1` — a retired hook name must not get a successful-looking reply), the `compass` module (its only caller was the gate), `backlog::find_open` plus `BacklogItem` (a queue reader with no consumer invites the next author to re-wire it), and the `backlog_prev_open`/`backlog_no_progress_streak` state fields (write-only once nothing observes the queue — serde keeps such fields invisible to the compiler, and a field claiming to count observations never made is the same drift as a stale comment). The Phase::Done latch changes its PREMISE and keeps resting on an observation: it was "condukt empty AND backlog empty", it is now "this condukt run has no pending task", whose `Determination::Undetermined` arm still blocks — Done is never reached by failing to look. Two tests were not deleted into silence but INVERTED on the same input, so the retirement is pinned rather than merely performed: a stub backlog answering with a pending item must now produce no block, no mention of the task, and no "/backlog" or "/flow" string (a re-worded nudge is still a nudge, which `blocks()` alone would miss), and an answer in an unrecognised status vocabulary — which used to block as undetermined — must now be ignored because no question is being asked. Kill power is measured, not argued: at 0ce4894a both old tests were green, and against this revision the same input yields "a readable, pending queue must drive /backlog, got: \"\"". `pending_run_state_still_drives_condukt` remains the anti-vacuity control, so "silent" here means "chose not to nudge", not "never ran". Session-end auto-flow gate: on Stop, prompt /record once, then loop /condukt and /backlog while work keeps *progressing* — continuation is progress-based (no call-count ceiling); stalled progress escalates *visibly* and the loop stops only when the pending/open set is empty. Subscription-native (one hook + bundled Rust binary, no API key). v0.1.19: an explicit user stop now stands the loop down for that Stop only — see `stop_intent`: if the user's most recent transcript signal (a typed message, or their answer to an `AskUserQuestion`) is an explicit stop instruction (e.g. "止めて"/"stop"), the Stop is allowed through untouched instead of blocking with a backlog/condukt nudge. Not a session-wide latch — no `Phase::Done` is set, so ordinary nagging resumes if the user keeps working afterward. v0.1.17: an observation autoflow could NOT make no longer reads as "no work left" — `backlog::find_open` / `condukt::find_pending` / `find_backlog_binary` now return `harness_core::verdict::Determination`, so an unreadable run-state, an unparseable or non-zero `backlog list`, a queue answering in an unknown status vocabulary, and an unlistable plugin-cache dir are `Undetermined` instead of an empty set. `Phase::Done` (a per-session silence latch) now requires an observed-empty queue; undetermined blocks visibly via `Verdict::stop_decision()`, and an undetermined binary lookup stands the auto-loop down instead of double-driving a live queue. v0.1.16: replaced the count-proxy stops with progress-based continuation (backlog 422d256a facets 822c7209/9aa0031f) — removed the condukt loop's auto-≤4×/ask-from-5× count split and the backlog loop's silent Phase::Done at max_backlog_prompts; both now continue while the remaining-work set shrinks and escalate visibly (never silently) via a no-progress streak vs cfg.stuck_threshold (default 3), consulting condukt state autonomy-check for the escalation wording. v0.1.15: strengthened the Tier 2 delegation-record advisory's own regression test (skill_doc_text_quoting_backlog_lock_acquire_never_fires) after an independent verifier found the prior fixture vacuous — no functional code change. v0.1.14: Tier 2 delegation-record advisory now matches only genuine executed Bash tool_use invocations (not raw transcript prose/doc text) and scopes run-completion checks to THIS session's own condukt run id (not the project-wide latest run file), fixing two false-positive classes (backlog d8051ed4). v0.1.9: Stop hook now runs under harness-core's run_guarded panic barrier (fail-closed block on crash instead of silent allow).

plugins.name: hypothesis
plugins.description: v0.1.13 adds the YAML frontmatter that skills/hypothesis/SKILL.md never had. Claude Code registers a skill from the frontmatter's name/description, so a file opening with prose is silently skipped: this skill was not broken, it was ABSENT (/hypothesis:hypothesis read as not found). The failure is invisible from the plugin's side -- the file is present, git status is clean, the rollout reports success -- which is the shape CLAUDE.md section 3 names, "was not registered" and "there was nothing to register" collapsing into one output. Measured 2026-08-26 at 58c779af, it was the only SKILL.md across all 39 crates whose first line was not `---`. plugins.name: propguard
plugins.description: v0.1.44 integrates this line with the remote's: the session-scoped skip now carries a third state. Session-scoping fixed WHOSE token is consumed; it did not fix WHEN. A Stop is adjudicated by four independent gate processes, so a token honoured by one that allows was burned even when another blocked the same stop — the stop never happened and the one-shot escape had been spent on nothing, which is standing pressure toward a permanent bypass (CLAUDE.md 5). `consume_session_skip` now takes `stop_hook_active` and parks an honoured token as `<id>.skip.honoured`: it is re-honoured while a re-entry after a block is in flight, and deleted the first time a chain actually ends. A rename failure that can neither bound nor clear the token is resolved to NOT honouring it. v0.1.41: the shared project-root `.propguard-skip` marker is gone. The operator escape is now `propguard skip --reason "..."`, which is scoped to the issuing session (CLAUDE.md 5 forbids a shared one-shot file under parallel sessions, since whichever session stops next consumes it), requires a non-empty reason, and appends both the issue and the consumption to the gate log so a bypass cannot happen unrecorded. v0.1.39: tests-only + comments for the v0.1.38 fix, after measuring that two of its four reads were unguarded. The untracked `ls-files` read's `Undetermined` forwarding arm had a kill rate of ZERO — replacing it with the pre-fix `Undetermined(_) => {}` kept all 97 tests green — so the 87dbfbb8 fail-open reopened through the untracked path: both `git diff` reads answer a legitimately empty string for an untracked file, the dropped `ls-files` failure leaves `others` empty, and `diff_text` hands back `Known("")` which the gate allows as `empty-diff`. Observed RED against exactly that shape (`got Known(DiffText { text: "", truncated: false })`) before the arm was restored. The fourth read (an untracked file's body) had only a unit test written WITH the fix that could never have been observed failing; it now also has a behavioural gate test, observed RED as `below-threshold` — i.e. pre-fix the gate JUDGED a diff whose only trace of the new file was a section header with no code under it. `diff_text` gained the same injectable-git seam `changed_files` already had (the real `git` will not fail `ls-files` while succeeding at `diff`, and the one real-git route — an untracked path whose name is not valid UTF-8 — is unbuildable on APFS: Errno 92). Each fault test ships with an anti-vacuity control on the same stand-in binary. Also corrected a false docstring: `a_genuinely_clean_repo_still_allows` claimed to catch a fix resolving "clean" to "undetermined", but the clean tree returns at `no-code-changes` and never calls `diff_text` (measured with a panic probe); the real pin is git.rs's `diff_text_of_an_unchanged_file_is_known_and_empty_not_undetermined`. `run_git` (thin wrapper) folded into `run_git_bin`, now the single choke point. No decision behavior change. v0.1.38: closes the fail-open v0.1.37 documented but deliberately left open (backlog 87dbfbb8 p0 + d8e22b26 p1). `run_git` now answers `Determination<String>` and `diff_text` answers `Determination<DiffText>`, forwarding (never re-minting) the boundary's `Undetermined` from any of the four reads that feed it: `git diff`, `git diff --cached`, the untracked `ls-files`, and an untracked file's body. `evaluate` maps that to a new `decide_diff_failed` — tag `diff-read-failed`, bounded by max_attempts, escapable, no hash recorded, no per-property violations attributed — placed BEFORE the `match cfg.mode` split so both inject and subprocess modes route through it. Measured before the fix with the real `git`: a tracked file whose working-tree content is not valid UTF-8 (no NUL, so git emits a textual diff) gave changed_files=Files(["bad.rs"]) with diff_text="" and truncated:false, and the gate returned ALLOW tag=empty-diff; the valid-UTF-8 control gave BLOCK tag=below-threshold. The partial case is closed the same way and deliberately returns no diff at all rather than the readable half: previously `git diff` succeeding while `git diff --cached` could not be decoded produced a diff mentioning a.rs, omitting b.rs, and carrying truncated:false — announcing itself complete over propguard's only incompleteness signal. `empty-diff` survives but now means only what it says: every read succeeded and the diff really was empty. New tests pin both faults end-to-end through `evaluate`, each with an anti-vacuity control that differs only in whether the bytes decode, plus a genuinely-clean-repo allow and a measured demonstration that Mode::Subprocess really can reach properties-satisfied (so the guard prevents a reachable allow, not a hypothetical one). Property gate for Claude Code: on Stop, derive 3–5 semantic properties (invariants) from a task's done_criteria and check the generated code against them before the agent can declare done. In inject mode it blocks and injects a property checklist for the running agent to self-verify (no API key); in subprocess mode it runs an independent checker and counts per-property PASS/FAIL, blocking when fewer than a threshold hold. Goes beyond 'concrete tests pass'. v0.1.36: an unreadable git stdout no longer reads as a clean repo — harness-core 0.2.3's bounded pipe read stopped discarding the read error and stopped folding an expired read budget into an empty string, so a `git` that exits 0 while its output never arrives now reaches ChangeScan::Failed (the gate fails closed) instead of the Files(vec![]) a genuinely clean repo produces. v0.1.32: fixed a stale never-break-a-turn docstring/comment in main.rs and README.md — panics no longer swallow-to-exit-0; the Stop hook's panic path resolves via harness_core::gate::run::run_guarded's fail-closed policy (block on the first stop, bounded allow only on a second consecutive stop_hook_active panic). No behavior change. v0.1.31: migrated run_checker's and run_git's independently-duplicated spawn+process-group-kill+bounded-timeout+bounded-stdout-read logic (CA-propguard-004/005/006) to the new shared harness_core::boundary::run_with_timeout / run_with_timeout_and_stdin primitive; local kill_checker_tree/kill_tree/read_stdout_bounded helpers removed, propguard's own wait-timeout dependency dropped (libc kept only for a test-only liveness probe). Existing timeout/kill/parse behavior preserved (all regression tests green). v0.1.29: cargo fmt fixup of a test fixture in derive.rs (no behavior change). v0.1.28: migrated 3 raw fs::read_to_string call sites (Config::load, source_criteria, diff_text's untracked-file read) to harness_core::boundary::read_to_string so an unreadable-but-existing file is distinguished from a genuinely absent one instead of both being silently folded together; existing fallback behavior at each site is unchanged. v0.1.27: fixed README.ja.md's stale doctrine — panics no longer swallow-to-exit-0; they resolve via harness_core::gate::run::run_guarded's fail-closed policy (block on first panic, bounded allow only on a second consecutive stop_hook_active panic). v0.1.16: merged two independently-developed Continuous-Audit fix lines that landed on the same v0.1.14 base — stopped correlation-store pollution (CA-propguard-03/04), and documented the checker subprocess timeout (checker_timeout_secs, default 300s, process-tree kill on timeout) with config-propagation tests. v0.1.13: fixed 3 subprocess-hang gaps (CA-propguard-004/005/006) — checker timeout now kills the whole shell-spawned process tree via a Unix process group, stdout reads are bounded so a lingering process can't hang them, and all git subprocess calls go through a timeout-bounded choke point with graceful fallback. Subscription-native, bundled Rust binary.

plugins.name: fetchguard
plugins.description: v0.1.2: DISCLOSES A PROTECTION GAP — doc-only, no logic change, and the gap is NOT closed by this version. Through 0.1.1 this crate was explicitly one half of a pair: it scans WHAT web-tool output says, and `taintguard` tracked WHERE content came from, downgrading write-class tools for the rest of a turn that had read something external. taintguard was removed from the repository on 2026-08-24 by user ruling. Its half is gone and was not reassigned, so: external-file `Read` (a path outside the project) now produces NO provenance signal and NO content scan, and nothing restricts the turn afterwards; and this crate's own enforcement is only an `additionalContext` warning — it downgrades and denies nothing. The prose that said the Read surface was "deferred to taintguard's provenance gate" (`gate.rs`'s fail-closed contract and `WEB_TOOLS`'s docstring) said the surface was covered elsewhere, which is now false; both, plus README.ja.md and the `scan`/`main` module docs, now state the surface is covered by nothing. Recorded as an open gap so it is visible rather than silently inherited. New crate (backlog 18506c09). Runtime content-level injection scanner: a PostToolUse hook (matcher WebFetch|WebSearch) scans the tool_response text for planted prompt-injection phrasings (concealment / verification-bypass / instruction-override / egress — the same four-category taxonomy scripts/check-prompt-injection.py already enforces at commit time) and, on a hit OR an undecidable response shape, injects additionalContext telling the model the flagged span is untrusted DATA whose embedded directives must NOT be followed. Closes the gap check-prompt-injection.py's own docstring names: that gate covers committed prompt assets, not text a web tool call pulls in at runtime. Orthogonal to taintguard's provenance signal (WHERE content came from) — this is the content signal (WHAT it says); the two are meant to run together. External-file Read is deferred (needs taintguard's path-trust classifier). A shared fixture corpus (scripts/tests/fixtures/injection_parity_corpus.json) is run by both this crate's tests/pattern_parity.rs and scripts/test_check_prompt_injection.py's ParityWithFetchguardCorpus, so the two independently-maintained taxonomies cannot silently drift apart. Subscription-native, bundled Rust binary (not yet registered in any enabledPlugins — building/merging this crate has no effect on a running session until a human does so and restarts).
